articles.title: 小米米家除螨仪 3 预售：升级 16kPa 吸力、双尘杯设计，券后 224 元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，小米推出米家除螨仪 3，现已开始全款预售，券后到手价 224 元。这款新品升级 16kPa 大吸力，内置高性能电机，能够高效吸除床褥中的尘螨、皮屑等多种脏污；升级双尘杯设计，储尘杯负责存储脏污，减少风道、旋风塔堵塞；过滤杯通过螺旋式气流剥离尘螨、皮屑等脏污，实现高效脏污气流分离。这款新品采用整机 6 重过滤，减少风道堵塞，不易跑尘，吸力更持久；支持每分钟 15,000 次高频强拍打，搭载三区共振拍打块，振动式拍打结构不易缠绕毛发；支持 LED 紫外线除菌，新增 65℃ 热风烘干功能，相比上一代温度提升 15℃，破坏螨虫生存环境，抑制螨虫滋生。IT之家附这款新品详细参数如下：京东小米米家除螨仪 3 券后 223.97 元领 25 元券京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 223 道题、2651 条标准：阿里 Qwen 开源 BlenderWorld，给 AI 出了一套 3D 建模大考
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，阿里 Qwen 团队于 10 月 14 日开源 BlenderWorld，这是一个用于评测视觉智能体在 Blender 中完成真实 3D 创作任务的基准。项目采用 MIT 许可证，代码与数据集已同步发布至 GitHub、Hugging Face 和 ModelScope。与常见的“生成一张图”不同，BlenderWorld 要求 AI 交付一个可编辑的 .blend 工程文件，并按需输出渲染图、视频或模型导出文件。在该测试中，模型不能只给出好看的画面，还要构建出材质、几何结构、灯光、相机等可被设计师继续修改的 3D 场景。该基准包含 223 个任务和 2,651 条标准，覆盖产品、建筑、自然环境、角色、动画和科学可视化等 9 大类、22 个子类。其中，78 个任务仅提供文字描述，130 个任务提供图片加文字，15 个任务提供视频加文字；另有 59 个任务附带尺寸、材质或相机参数等规格文件。评测方式也颇为严格：系统会从 8 个自适应视角渲染提交的 Blender 项目，并结合场景检查、2,651 条任务专属二元评分标准，以及 8 项整体视觉质量评分。最终成绩由规则符合度与视觉质量各占 50% 加权得出。该项目目前已提供完整的安装、生成、打包和评测流程，支持开发者将任意生成框架接入测试。仓库显示其采用 Blender 4.2.10，并需要 Linux、Python 3.10 及以上环境；评测环节还需配置具备视觉能力的模型服务。IT之家附上参考点此前往 GitHub 访问 BlenderWorld

articles.title: 三星电子美国泰勒第二晶圆厂计划 2026 年 11 月动工
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，据得克萨斯州媒体《奥斯汀美国政治家报》当地时间本月 15 日报道，三星奥斯汀与泰勒工厂负责人 Jon Taylor 在一次媒体活动中确认，泰勒市集群的第二座晶圆厂 (Fab 2) 计划于 2026 年 11 月动工。Jon Taylor 同时提到，泰勒 Fab 1 仍将按计划于 2026 年内上线。该晶圆厂自今年春季以来持续开展设备导入工作，现在已进入验证阶段，当前气体和化学品几乎全数投用，已安装的设备开始运行。这位三星电子高管感谢 Tesla（特斯拉）的订单，并表示 Elon Musk（埃隆 · 马斯克）的 Terafab 计划不会改变这笔交易。参考https://www.statesman.com/business/technology/article/samsung-taylor-ai-chip-demand-22475945.php

articles.title: 古尔曼称苹果调整法律团队：从 Meta 挖来诉讼主管，出任全球诉讼与金融服务副总裁
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，彭博社的马克 · 古尔曼（Mark Gurman）今日发文，据知情人士透露，苹果公司聘请了斯科特 · 塔克（Scott Tucker），他是 Meta 的副总法律顾问兼诉讼主管。这一人事变动让塔克与苹果新任总法律顾问詹妮弗 · 纽斯特德（Jennifer Newstead）再度联手 —— 纽斯特德从老东家 Meta 直接引进了自己此前信赖的副手。知情人士表示，塔克将出任苹果全球诉讼与金融服务副总裁，这是一个新设立的职位，监管公司在全球范围内的商业及专利诉讼，还将负责处理与苹果金融产品相关的法律事务。IT之家从报道获悉，随着这一任命落地，苹果现任商业与竞争诉讼副总裁希瑟 · 格雷尼尔（Heather Grenier）的汇报层级有所下移，改为向塔克汇报，而不再直接向纽斯特德汇报；不过，格雷尼尔仍将保留在纽斯特德的法务核心领导层内。除在 Meta 的任职经历外，塔克此前还曾担任摩根士丹利高级法律职务，这些经验与他新负责的金融服务领域高度契合。纽斯特德在 Meta 担任首席法律高管六年，并于今年 3 月出任苹果公司总法律顾问。与此同时，苹果法务部门的另一位资深成员、长期负责监管及产品相关法律事务的副总裁凯尔 · 安德尔（Kyle Andeer），其管辖权责也进一步扩大。他将接管国际法律事务，并全面监管涉及儿童网络安全、网络安全保障以及执法合规合作等业务板块。苹果与 Meta 的发言人均对此拒绝置评。上述人事调整属于纽斯特德主导的更广泛组织重组的一部分，目前她全面统辖苹果的法律与政府事务团队。苹果近期还聘请了前美国航空集团高管内特 · 加滕（Nate Gatten）担任政府事务副总裁，并在多个海外区域任命了新的政府事务主管。在环境、政策及社会倡议事务前负责人丽莎 · 杰克逊（Lisa Jackson）和前首席法务官凯特 · 亚当斯（Kate Adams）相继退休后，苹果将法律团队与政府事务团队整合归入纽斯特德麾下。目前转任公司执行董事长的原首席执行官蒂姆 · 库克，也在政府事务领域扮演着核心领导角色。当前苹果深陷多条司法战线，包括美国司法部发起的一项重磅反垄断诉讼、与 Epic Games 就 App Store 抽成限制展开的长年纠纷，以及围绕用户隐私与 Siri 功能推迟交付的相关诉讼。近年来，苹果面临的裁决赔偿与和解金额累计已高达数十亿美元，欧美监管机构也对其支撑商业模式的核心业务行为展开了轮番调查与施压。部分苹果高管认为，公司在法庭诉讼中的表现未达预期，尤其是在 App Store 相关诉讼中处于被动。这些法律挫折迫使苹果调整其佣金分成比例及向开发者收费的边界条件，这也为近年来作为苹果核心增长引擎的服务业务蒙上了增速明显放缓的阴影。服务业务增长遇阻，将对苹果整体的财务表现带来沉重打击。即便是放在常态时期，统管苹果庞大的诉讼业务也是一项极其棘手的工作。这家总部位于加州库比蒂诺的科技巨头是全球遭遇诉讼最频繁的企业之一，案情跨度极大 —— 从零售门店发生的顾客滑倒摔伤索赔，到涉案金额达数十亿美元的重磅反垄断纠纷，不一而足。最近数周，新任 CEO 特努斯主导了一系列大刀阔斧的高管重组，包括为 App Store、大型发布活动，以及信息安全与房地产等公司职能部门调派新负责人。这轮人事洗牌还涉及任职多年的 Apple Pay 负责人离职、更换公司并购（M&A）主管，以及对硬件工程部门架构的大规模调整。

articles.title: ChatGPT 能替你操作谷歌 Chrome 浏览器了：读网页、网购比价、发消息等
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，OpenAI 于 10 月 15 日更新 ChatGPT for Chrome 扩展程序（版本号 1.26.1005.11759），ChatGPT 现在可以读取 Chrome 浏览器中已打开的多个标签页，并基于这些网页内容回答问题、整理信息或完成跨页面任务。该功能面向所有用户开放，无论是否订阅付费服务均可使用。用户在聊天中调用浏览器后，ChatGPT 可将当前打开的网页作为上下文，例如比较多个商品页面、汇总多份资料或分析工作文档。IT之家援引博文介绍，此次更新还引入了更强的“操作”能力。在 Work 模式下，ChatGPT 不再仅限于阅读网页，而是可以在获得授权后控制标签页，帮助用户填写表单、发送消息、下载文件、整理和分组标签页等。由于扩展程序运行在用户常用的浏览器配置中，它能够复用用户已登录网站的登录状态，从而在 Gmail、LinkedIn、Salesforce 或企业内部工具等场景中直接协助处理工作流程。不过，便利背后是更大的权限要求。安装或启用相关能力后，Chrome 可能要求扩展程序读取和修改网站数据、访问页面调试工具、管理标签页和下载内容，甚至读取书签、浏览历史或显示通知。OpenAI 表示，这些权限是让 ChatGPT 操作浏览器所必需的，但用户仍可通过逐站授权、允许名单、阻止名单等方式控制其访问范围。默认情况下，ChatGPT 在接触每个新网站前都会请求确认，用户可选择“仅允许一次”“对该网站始终允许”“对所有网站始终允许”或拒绝。其中，“对所有网站始终允许”被 OpenAI 标记为较高风险选项；浏览历史和文件上传、下载也需单独授权。

articles.title: OpenAI 升级适用于谷歌 Chrome 浏览器的 ChatGPT 扩展：能直接读取你的标签页
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，当地时间 16 日，OpenAI 宣布升级 Chrome 浏览器的 ChatGPT 扩展程序，支持读取用户打开的标签页，提供更有针对性的回答。OpenAI 曾推出自有浏览器，随后又于 8 月 9 日停用。此后，公司持续改进 Chrome 扩展程序，增强 ChatGPT 在浏览器中的竞争力。最新一轮升级，进一步扩展了 ChatGPT 在 Chrome 中的功能。在 ChatGPT 聊天模式下，用户可以让 AI 助手查看 Chrome 中打开的网页，并根据其中的内容回答问题。例如，在三个标签页中分别打开不同的沙发商品页面后，用户可以直接让 ChatGPT 比较尺寸、价格、送货时间和退货政策。使用面向复杂任务的 ChatGPT Work 时，用户还可以让 AI 助手代发消息、填写表格或整理标签页。例如，让 ChatGPT 填写新牙医要求的表格，再把日程添加到日历；或者分析多个标签页中几家承包商的服务条款，再给最符合自己需求的服务商拟一封邮件。据IT之家了解，Chrome 侧边栏中的 ChatGPT 也获得了访问全部聊天记录的能力。用户不必离开正在浏览的网页，就能继续与 ChatGPT 对话或安排任务。ChatGPT 扩展程序面向所有套餐开放。OpenAI 称，除 Chrome 外，微软 Edge、Brave 和 Opera 等基于 Chromium 的浏览器也能使用该扩展程序。

articles.title: IDC 等机构谈苹果首款折叠 iPhone Duo：首发难抢，今年出货预估 600~700 万台
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，CNBC 今天（10 月 17 日）发布博文，采访了 Counterpoint Research、IDC、TechInsights 以及摩根大通等机构分析师，围绕着苹果公司首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo，探讨预测该机未来销量趋势。Counterpoint 研究总监 Tarun Pathak 预测 iPhone Duo 初期需求会超过供应。Pathak 认为目前苹果 iPhone 的整体存量大约达到 14 亿部，即便是很小比例的早期用户选择尝鲜，短期内预估会有约 600 万潜在买家。市场研究机构 IDC 认为，折叠屏并非全新技术，安卓厂商已布局多年。苹果的真正机会在于，将这一形态带给其庞大的 iPhone 生态用户。IDC 预计，今年折叠屏手机约占全球智能手机出货量的 2%，却贡献接近 7% 的行业收入；到 2030 年，其收入占比有望升至 10%，但出货量占比仍仅约 3%。IDC 预计苹果今年约出货 700 万部 iPhone Duo，明年出货量或再增长 70%，届时可能占据全球折叠屏市场约 40% 份额，超过三星和华为。摩根大通则认为，即便明年 iPhone 总出货量大致持平，Duo 仍可能凭借更高的平均售价，对 iPhone 收入产生不成比例的拉动。该行判断，iPhone 18 周期的增长将更多来自价格与产品组合。不过，风险同样存在。TechInsights 分析师指出，在消费者换机周期不断拉长、全球智能手机增长放缓的背景下，更贵的 iPhone 可能促使部分用户进一步推迟升级，形成“价格越高、换机越慢、需求越弱”的循环。

articles.title: 昔年“彩电一哥”谢幕：康佳确定退市，连续 4 年累亏约 203 亿元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，*ST 康佳 A (000016.SZ) 昨日（10 月 16 日）发布公告，称深交所《关于康佳集团股份有限公司股票终止上市的决定》（深证上〔2026〕1,390 号），深交所决定终止公司股票上市。深交所决定终止康佳集团人民币普通股（A 股）ST 康佳 A 及境内上市外资股（B 股）*ST 康佳 B 的上市，证券代码分别为 000,016、200,016。根据公告，本次终止上市源于公司以股东会决议方式主动申请终止股票上市。2026 年 9 月 14 日，康佳集团召开 2026 年第二次临时股东会，审议通过相关议案；公司随后于 9 月 23 日向深交所提交申请材料，深交所于 9 月 28 日受理。深交所依据《深圳证券交易所股票上市规则（2026 年修订）》第 9.7.1 条第一款第一项、第 9.7.9 条第二款及上市审核委员会审议意见，作出终止上市决定。由于属于上市公司主动终止上市，按照规则第 9.7.11 条，公司股票不进入退市整理期。公告显示，ST 康佳 A、ST 康佳 B 将自深交所公告终止上市决定之日起 5 个交易日内摘牌。终止上市后，公司股份将转入全国中小企业股份转让系统依托原证券公司代办股份转让系统设立的“两网公司及退市公司”板块挂牌转让；公司已聘请江海证券担任代办机构。康佳集团曾被称为“彩电第一股”，近年经营承压。公开报道显示，公司连续四年累计亏损约 203 亿元，并出现资不抵债情况。此次主动退市意味着其将告别深交所主板，后续股东需关注退市板块的股份流动性、转让安排及公司经营与重整进展。IT之家附上相关公告如下：

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，韩媒首尔经济日报昨日报道称，三星在为 Galaxy S27 Ultra 手机做最终性能验证时，发现高通第六代骁龙 8 超级至尊版芯片在高负载运行时温度反复超过阈值，导致出现降频。高通公司首席营销官莫珂东（Don McGuire）随后在 X 平台表示，（该消息）完全不准确（100% NOT accurate）。莫珂东随后进行了详细说明，他表示骁龙 8 Elite Gen 6（IT之家注：此处应指系列芯片，包含第六代骁龙 8 至尊版、第六代骁龙 8 超级至尊版两款芯片）不存在系统性散热问题：OEM 厂商在筹备产品发布期间，会持续对芯片平台进行优化调整，针对不同的使用场景，力求在性能与功耗之间取得平衡。我们（与 OEM 厂商）携手合作，致力于为用户提供最佳体验。

articles.title: 存储器、E-Glass 双面夹击成本，传三星 MX 2027 年智能手机业务计划悬而未决
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，韩媒 ZDNET Korea 当地时间本月 15 日报道称，三星电子 MX 业务不仅下调了 2026Q4 的智能手机 MX 产量预测，还未能按惯例及时发布 2027 年智能手机业务计划，导致上游供应商也面临不确定性。三星 MX 之所以尚未发布明年计划，是因为其成本结构由于存储器、E-Glass 价格的上涨持续恶化，导致必须在中低端机型的销量和整体盈利能力之间进行取舍。▲ 图源：日东纺E-Glass 玻璃纤维是智能手机用 CCL（覆铜板）的关键组成，而 CCL 又是 PCB（印刷电路板）的核心材料。三星 MX 的 E-Glass 供应高度依赖业界龙头日东纺 (Nittobo)，但日东纺正将其有限的产能更多地分配到适用于 AI 半导体、盈利能力更为出色的 T-Glass 低热膨胀系数玻纤布上，这意味着 E-Glass 供应紧张、价格上涨。参考https://zdnet.co.kr/view/?no=20261015164031

articles.title: 苹果 App Store 新规落地，AI 深度伪造迎来最严审核
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，苹果公司昨日（10 月 16 日）更新《App 审核指南》，在最新修订的 1.2 条款中，加强治理针对 AI 内容创作类应用，将 AI 生成的、未经当事人同意的私密图像明确纳入禁止范围。IT之家附上修订内容如下：1.2 用户生成内容对于包含用户生成内容的 App，有特定的难题需要解决，比如知识产权侵权、未经同意传播私密图像、匿名欺凌等。为了避免滥用，包含用户生成内容或社交网络服务的 App 必须满足以下条件：采用相应的方法来过滤令人反感的内容，以免这些内容在 App 中发布制定一个机制，以举报攻击性内容并在出现问题时及时作出回应若用户发布攻击性内容，可以取消其使用服务的资格公布联系信息，以便用户与你联系科技媒体 9to5Mac 指出，此次调整的直接背景，是近一年围绕 App Store 的多起争议。科技透明度项目曾发现数十款 AI“裸体化”应用，并指出 App Store 的搜索建议和广告也会把用户导向这类应用；旧金山官员随后要求苹果下架 8 款可生成未经同意私密图像的应用。此外用户曾投诉 xAI 的 Grok 聊天机器人被用于制作裸露或性化深度伪造图像；今年早些时候，苹果曾警告 xAI，若继续放任此类内容，将把 Grok 从 App Store 下架。xAI 随后增设防护机制，更新版本才获得批准。苹果还新增 2.5.19 条准则，禁止应用在审核时隐瞒真实功能、通过后再加入“裸露化”（nudify）等有害能力。这类“先过审、后解锁”的做法被称为“诱饵式营销”，今后可能导致应用下架，开发者也可能被终止 Apple Developer Program 资格。此外，苹果将禁止助长人口贩卖或剥削儿童的应用的范围，扩展至替代应用分发渠道，并表示对违规应用和开发者“不会犹豫”采取下架或终止合作等措施。

articles.content: “IT早报”时间，大家好，现在是 2026 年 10 月 17 日星期六，今天的重要科技资讯有：1. 苹果首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 预约火爆，官网排到明年发货国行定价 15999 元起，开抢后渠道一度卡顿，目前 2026 年备货已售罄，部分机型发货排到明年 1 月，该机维修价格最高近 8000 元。>> 查看详情2. “疯狂小杨哥”张庆杨宣布复播：注销原抖音账号，启用新号“庆杨”声明称，“疯狂小杨哥”账号停播以来，其就直播中存在的违规行为进行了深刻反省，并经过两年认真整改。按照法律法规和平台规则，现注销原账号，注册新账号“庆杨”复播，将更加专注于内容创作和自营品牌运营。>> 查看详情3. 这次能飞了！特斯拉第二代 Roadster 跑车正式亮相根据介绍，2008 年的 Roadster 只有一个目标：证明电动汽车可以速度飞快、外形性感、引人期待，而 10 月 16 日发布的第二代 Roadster，则展现了历史上的一个新时刻：最后几辆人类驾驶汽车之中的佼佼者。>> 查看详情4. 国铁集团启动全国铁路列车车次编排改革：旅客列车增改 X、T、K、N、V 等字头字母，信息更直观新版列车车次做了全面系统优化调整，其中动车组旅客列车车次的字头字母由原来的 4 个增加至 7 个，可编排的列车车次数量增长近 40%。>> 查看详情5. 苹果库克：iPhone Duo 完全在中国制造，非常期待它在中国市场的表现10 月 15 日，在 iPhone Duo 即将开售之际，库克表示，自己每次用它都忍不住嘴角上扬，非常期待它在中国市场的表现。>> 查看详情6. 抖音：经有关部门批准，同意三只羊注销原账号、注册新账号、发布内容和恢复经营抖音宣布，按照相关法律法规及平台规则，并经有关部门批准，同意三只羊公司在抖音平台上注销原账号、注册新账号、发布内容和恢复经营。>> 查看详情7. 苹果库克时隔 3 年再次现身米哈游总部，与“大伟哥”见面多位网友 10 月 16 日晒出视频，苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆 · 库克现身上海米哈游总部，米哈游创始人、总裁刘伟（大伟哥）亲自接待。>> 查看详情8. 消息称 DeepSeek 将 Harness、Web、App、Platform 团队整合成立“产品部”有消息称 DeepSeek 最近将 Harness 团队以及 Web、App、Platform 团队整合成“产品部”，负责公司的所有的产品、设计和研发工作，崔添翼任产品部负责人。>> 查看详情9. 马斯克：第二代 Roadster 将是最后一款“人工驾驶”特斯拉车型特斯拉希望将 Roadster 打造成旗下的性能旗舰。新车采用了多项技术，能够在加速、过弯和综合性能方面达到惊人水平。>> 查看详情10. 马斯克回应第二代 Roadster 跑车能否合法上路：能不能要看道路情况汽车媒体 insideevs 10 月 16 日发布博文，报道称针对车主最关心的第二代 Roadster 跑车能否合法上路，全球首富埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）并未给出明确答案，并解读认为可能仅适用于私人场地以及部分支持地区。>> 查看详情11. 库克卸任苹果 CEO 后首次中国之行结束：期待下次再见苹果董事会执行主席、前 CEO 蒂姆 · 库克 10 月 16 日发文告别本次中国之行，并分享视频。值得一提的是，这也是库克卸任苹果 CEO 后首次中国之行。>> 查看详情12. 重庆车企赛力斯频遭网络谣言，全国各地公安机关已依法查处 22 名违法行为人10 月 15 日，重庆市公安局沙坪坝区分局微信公号“平安沙坪坝”发布通报，公布 3 起涉企网络谣言、网络暴力典型案例。据重庆日报报道，3 起案件的受害企业均为重庆本土车企赛力斯集团股份有限公司。针对赛力斯的网络谣言、网络暴力案件，全国各地公安机关已依法查处了 22 名违法行为人，其中重庆警方查处 7 名，外地警方查处 15 名。>> 查看详情13. 卢伟冰晒小米 REDMI K100 真机，称将把旗舰的起点再往上提高一大步10 月 16 日上午，小米集团合伙人、总裁，手机部总裁、小米品牌总经理卢伟冰在B站发视频进一步预告 REDMI K100 标准版新机，并放出了绿色的真机外观。>> 查看详情14. 今年势头最猛的国产旗舰：消息称华为 Pura X View 阔直板手机出货量超 71 万，实销均价在 7000 元左右博主 @数码闲聊站 爆料，渠道数据显示，华为阔直板（Pura X View）出货量已超 71 万，实销均价在 7000 元左右，其中约 30％用户来自苹果用户。>

articles.title: Anthropic 内部调查：大多数员工相信到 2030 年 AI 能完成至少八成工作
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，据《商业内幕》今天（17 日）早间报道，Anthropic 员工普遍认为，AI 将取代自己大部分工作，绝大多数美国劳动者则持不同看法。Anthropic 最新研究对比了美国成年人和 1334 名公司员工的调查结果。大多数 Anthropic 员工预计，到 2030 年，自己至少 80% 的工作可以交给 AI 完成，而美国劳动者中只有约 5% 的人持相同看法。研究反映出 Anthropic 员工与普通美国人对 AI 未来发展的判断存在巨大差异。对于 AI 能力的进步速度、节省工作时间的效果，以及未来经济增长的速度，Anthropic 员工的预期都乐观得多。以调查结果的中位数计算，Anthropic 员工预计，到 2030 年底，开发一款新 AI 模型所需的工作中，95% 可以由 AI 完成。Anthropic 首席经济学家彼得 · 麦克罗里认为，员工们的判断或许能帮助外界为更先进的 AI 做好准备：“我们发表这项研究，是因为 Anthropic 在 AI 应用方面比整个经济体系领先约一年半。换句话说，Anthropic 内部发生的变化，可能预示着整个社会接下来会发生什么。”Anthropic 还调查了劳动者使用 AI 的情况及对 AI 未来影响的看法。研究显示，美国成年人和 Anthropic 员工对 AI 目前能做什么，基本有着相同的认识。但对于 AI 进步有多快、应用会有多广泛，以及能节省多少时间、提高多少生产率，双方的看法存在分歧。IT之家从报道中获悉，造成上述差异的原因可能不止一个。Anthropic 员工可以获得更多使用 AI 工具的预算，还经常有机会试用尚未公开发布的模型。相比之下，普通美国劳动者从事体力劳动或服务业工作的比例更高。调查显示，技工、生产和运输行业的劳动者认为，到 2030 年，AI 能够接手的工作比例相对最低。Anthropic 员工、科技行业从业者以及商业和金融业受访者则预计，AI 将承担更多工作。就业前景方面，大多数 Anthropic 员工预计，美国失业率将在 2030 年超过 12%；多数美国劳动者则认为，届时失业率不会超过 8%，或者维持在 8% 左右。美国当前的失业率为 4.2%。对于 AI 究竟会给就业市场带来多大冲击，现有研究尚未得出一致结论。Anthropic 研究人员还利用问卷回答推算了受访者对经济增长的预期。以中位数计算，美国成年人对应的 2030 年 GDP 增速为 5.4%，Anthropic 员工则高达 17.1%。作为对比，美国去年 GDP 增长了 2.2%。

articles.title: 蒲得宇预估 2026 全球手机出货量降 14.2%，苹果成唯一增长的主要手机厂商
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，在本周发布的投资简报中，广发证券分析师蒲得宇（Jeff Pu）和 Henry Huang 预测，苹果将是 2026 年唯一一家出货量实现增长的主要智能手机制造商（增长 4%）。在两位分析师联合发布的投资简报中，预测 2026 年全球智能手机出货量约 10.8 亿部，同比下降约为 14.2%。而苹果却有望成为唯一实现出货增长的主要厂商，达到 2.57 亿部，预计同比增长 4%，届时其全球出货份额将从 2025 年的 20% 升至 24%，继续领先三星（2.41 亿部）。投资简报中，预估 2026 年三星和华为品牌手机出货量和 2025 年持平，同比增长均为 0%，而其它手机厂商会出现不同程度的下降情况。报告认为，内存价格大幅上涨正在挤压整个行业：手机厂商被迫削减出货计划、提高售价，2026 至 2027 年或成为行业最艰难的阶段之一。苹果凭借更强的品牌溢价、产品组合与供应链能力，相对更能抵御这轮下行压力。不过，苹果并非没有隐忧。分析师指出，iPhone 18 Pro 与 iPhone 18 Pro Max 市场反响相对平淡，部分原因包括 iPhone Duo 的竞争，以及用户对其机身重量的批评。受可调光圈摄像头相关限制影响，iPhone 18 Pro 系列的 2026 年生产计划被下调至 7,200 万部。iPhone Duo 也遭遇铰链供应瓶颈，2026 年 EMS 生产计划由 700 万部下调至 600 万部。该机型已开始预订，起售价 1,999 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 13,399 元人民币），美国市场的预计交付时间已延至 1 月底，部分地区更晚，显示需求旺盛但产能吃紧。资本市场方面，该报告维持苹果股票“持有”评级，目标价 369 美元（现汇率约合 2,473 元人民币）。苹果当日收于 343.46 美元（现汇率约合 2,302 元人民币），上涨 0.43%，成为科技板块普遍抛售中唯一收涨的主要科技股。IT之家援引图文内容，附上相关表格情况如下：季度出货量厂商 / articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，易速马 (EasySMX) 现已启动赤兔 S05 Pro 手柄的预售。这一控制器面向任天堂 Nintendo Switch 1/2 平台，支持三模连接，搭载 TMR 摇杆，标配智能启停充电底座，到手价 219 元。S05 Pro 配备两段式霍尔效应传感器扳机、静音导电硅胶 ABXY、M1&M2 自定义小肩键，集成四马达双区震动、六轴陀螺仪，可一键唤醒两代 Nintendo Switch 游戏主机，支持 amiibo NFC 识别，集成 RGB 灯带。该手柄本体三维 160×110×80 (mm)，内置 1000mAh 电池，本体质量 262g，可选晨曦蓝、暗夜黑配色。京东易速马 S05 Pro 手柄 249 元直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 零跑改造 43 年欧宝工厂造电车，首台欧洲制造零跑 B10 正式下线
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，零跑汽车宣布，10 月 16 日，零跑西班牙马连（Mallén）电池工厂正式投产，零跑西班牙萨拉戈萨工厂首台欧洲制造零跑 B10 正式下线，官方称之为“零跑改造 43 年欧宝工厂造电车”。IT之家获悉，萨拉戈萨工厂拥有 43 年的汽车制造历史，累计生产汽车超过 1000 万辆，具备深厚的工业积淀与成熟的制造基础。目前，零跑 B10 正式加入该工厂的生产体系，与欧宝 Corsa、标致 208 和蓝旗亚 Ypsilon 共同生产。为适应 B10 的生产需求，零跑与 Stellantis 集团工程团队共同推进产线适配，在西班牙马连打造本地化电池组装基地。据介绍，零跑西班牙电池工厂专注于电池模组组装及相关关键工序。通过整车制造与电池配套相结合，零跑在西班牙逐步形成更贴近当地生产需求的制造协作体系，共同支撑零跑车型的欧洲本土生产。

articles.title: 英监管机构拟认定微软商业软件“垄断地位”，或干预旗下产品捆绑销售
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，据路透社 16 日报道，英国竞争与市场管理局拟认定微软在商业软件市场具有“战略市场地位”，此举可能使监管机构有权干预微软将 Excel、Teams 及 AI 助手 Copilot 等产品捆绑销售的做法。今年 5 月，英国竞争与市场管理局开始调查微软在商业软件市场的地位是否妨碍竞争。据悉，微软的商业软件在英国每月约有 2000 万用户。监管机构当天指出，微软在 PC 操作系统以及办公、安全、服务器和数据库管理软件市场均占据强势地位，客户转用其他供应商的产品时面临诸多障碍，进一步巩固了微软的市场优势。微软发言人不认同这一结论：“我们的所有产品，包括 Copilot，都采用开放设计，能够与其他服务互通，客户可以同时使用微软产品和竞争对手的服务。”英国竞争与市场管理局接下来将调查客户能否自由选择 AI 工具，以及其他厂商能否与 Copilot 展开竞争。据IT之家了解，监管机构还将审查微软将安全软件与其他产品捆绑销售的做法是否限制客户选择，以及软件授权方式如何影响客户选择云服务。英国竞争与市场管理局 CEO 莎拉 · 卡德尔说，从小型企业到重要公共服务机构，英国各地的工作场所都离不开商业软件和云服务。“企业和机构应该能够选择最适合自己的产品，需要时可以更换供应商，也可以同时使用不同供应商的服务。我们希望确保企业能够自由决定如何将微软产品与其他产品搭配使用。”英国竞争与市场管理局将就这项提议征求各方意见，并在 2027 年 2 月前作出最终决定。如果提议获得通过，微软将成为第三家受到英国数字市场新监管制度约束的企业。此前，谷歌因网络搜索业务被认定具有战略市场地位；2025 年 10 月，谷歌和苹果的移动平台也获得同样认定。监管机构还指出，微软和亚马逊云科技（AWS）仍需进一步消除客户更换云服务商、同时使用多家云服务商时面临的障碍。两家公司采取了一些措施来增加客户的选择，这其中包括推动各自的数据中心与竞争对手互联，以及免除客户更换云服务商时的数据传输费用。对此，监管机构认为，仍有改进余地。英国竞争与市场管理局将继续与两家公司合作，同时评估是否需要对云服务行业启动正式调查。微软发言人称：“我们欢迎英国竞争与市场管理局承认，微软在云服务市场的地位不足以成为依据数字市场竞争制度认定其具有战略市场地位的理由。”AWS 同样对监管机构公布的最新进展表示欢迎：“2026 年，我们持续投资开发 AI、多云服务和开放标准方面的新功能，让客户在构建和运营系统时拥有更大的自主权。”

articles.title: 非磁吸 / 卡扣：苹果 79 美元 iPhone Duo 手机壳靠胶条固定
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 17 日消息，科技媒体 MacRumors 昨日（10 月 16 日）发布博文，报道称适用于苹果首款折叠 iPhone Duo 的官方手机壳（售价为 79 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 529.5 元人民币））并未采用常规的卡扣或磁吸方式固定，从曝光的上手图片来看采用胶条方案，引发不少科技用户讨论。这款保护壳由左右两部分组成，内侧边缘配有黏性胶条。用户需撕掉胶条保护膜，将两半分别贴合到 iPhone Duo 上，并按压确保牢固粘合。它采用聚碳酸酯材质，提供沙色和海军蓝两种配色，主要保护机身背面摄像头凸起区域及外屏四周。与另一款产品相比，这一设计显得较为特殊。苹果同时销售的 iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand 售价 129 美元（现汇率约合 864.7 元人民币），采用磁吸固定，不使用粘合剂；但它不能保护机身侧面，使用时也会遮挡正面外屏，需要时可通过磁吸向后翻折。不少用户担心，粘合剂方案会降低更换手机壳的便利性，长期使用后胶条粘性可能下降，也可能在机身与壳体之间积累灰尘或残留胶痕。

articles.title: Emu Concept – Make AI Follows Your Rules. (Feedback Wanted)
articles.content:
The idea is how can we make personal agent apps on the phone just listen to your rules... Like it's weird to have Muse, Grok Bot, Dots, Instinct not ask me about when I want them to work for me or align with my rules, values, and goals.If I give these agents access to tools/connectors/data they just "assume" what I want or what it should do rather than asking me? And even if I set these for a specific agent then what happens when a newer personal agent comes out? Do I have to reconfigure again my rules for each flavor of personal agents or harness?This is where our initial idea stems from and we need feedback:Emu is a self-learning on-device AI guardian that makes AI agents follow your rules. Also the video above kind of just highlights Emu's concept thought process.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20665v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. articles.content:

Abstract: Rapid advances in AI capabilities are causing benchmarks to saturate. Once several models approach perfect scores, a benchmark loses its power to differentiate between them, and with it its utility for informing AI safety cases and frontier policies. Abstract: Reward-guided discrete diffusion enables test-time alignment with downstream objectives, but applying Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) guidance at every denoising step is computationally expensive. Abstract: Representation-based safety defenses for vision-language models (VLMs) often learn to separate harmful from benign inputs, but separation alone does not establish what a risk score means or when it should be trusted. Abstract: Formal inequality proving requires mathematical reasoning and exact computation, often connected through intermediate lemmas and goal reformulations. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20685v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic regression searches for an equation that explains observed data. Numerical error is commonly used to guide the search, but it alone can favor an accurate surrogate over a candidate with the right structure. We propose L2G-SR, a framework for LLM-based symbolic regression that guides search with a learned structural verifier. We construct structural supervision signal using tree edit distance (TED), accounting for commutative operators and alternative expression forms. A verifier first aligns numerical observations with the formulas, then learns to score a candidate's structural similarity to the target formula. At search time, the target formula is hidden and the verifier complements numerical error in parent selection. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20764v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper challenges the understanding capabilities of existing AI paradigms and emerging world models by asking a fundamental question: How quickly can reality change before an intelligent system can no longer reliably perceive, reason, and act? arXiv:2610.20780v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), a local mistake can propagate as other agents build on it, turning a correctable error into a failed task. Diagnosing completed runs or repeatedly re-executing them to search for corrections does not provide a learned policy for intervening while execution is still in progress. We present Agent Runtime Inspection and Amendment (ARIA), a framework for learning when and how to repair ongoing multi-agent executions. Our key intuition is to turn execution-verified repairs into reusable supervision, moving repair search into data construction and training so that a learned model can intervene at runtime without repeatedly testing alternatives. articles.title: Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The closed world asks AI for specialized competence and lets it manufacture the iid data its theory assumes: a fixed criterion licenses collecting examples until the task is covered. The open world asks for versatility --- taking up tasks a machine was not built for, from few examples and with little prior from a human designer --- and offers data that is grouped, not shuffled. Its tasks are not known in advance, so a machine must do inference-time learning (1st requirement). Modeling tasks as sharing latent factors and decomposing the training objective, we derive two more: a *rich representation*, retaining more than iid generalization requires, and a predictive disentanglement that aligns inputs and outputs into matched low-dimensional groups. Abstract: Multi-modal agents have made significant progress in interacting with open worlds. However, their ability to self-evolve remains limited. Supervised fine-tuning enables imitation but not active experience organization, while outcome-based reinforcement learning promotes exploration yet underuses intermediate trajectory information. Therefore, we propose EvolvingBrain, which uses an adaptive skill system as the brain for agent self-evolution, consisting of two following components. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20805v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A reasoning trace retained at answer time plays two roles: it can raise accuracy, and it can compete with the current evidence when the two disagree. We disentangle these roles by crossing verified evidence versions with the traces generated from each and answering from the same traces and evidence under two configurations: continuation of the model's own thinking and a separate answer call. Across three model families (gpt-oss, Gemma4, Qwen3) on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, the separate call raises evidence-following over continuation by 29.9 to 60.6 points. On the same pairs, removing the trace lowers accuracy by similar amounts under both configurations. Yet continuation repeats the stale conclusion in most conflicts, and the separate call follows the current evidence far more often. Abstract: A self-improving agent has to decide which new skills to keep, and in practice it keeps whatever earns a high reward, convinces a judge model, or compresses its library, even when the skill is wrong. We ask a harder question: can an agent grow what it can compute with no reward, no judge, and no answer key, and still be exactly right? The inner loop answers new questions only when two independently written expressions agree on every record. Abstract: Text-to-video models often generate the visual concepts requested in natural language prompts but fail to satisfy their intended ordering, timing, and persistence requirements. articles.content:

Abstract: Evaluator-guided reasoning presents a local control problem at every step: trust the current answer, return a fallback, or spend more inference. A local action-gap analysis characterizes when score errors can change a decision, while an expected regret bound accounts for errors along the realized expansion path. Guided by this analysis, we learn and calibrate action-specific confidence estimates, with local uncertainty penalties for ambiguous decisions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20845v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Skill-policy co-evolution, in which an agent's policy model and its skill bank improve each other during training, is a promising paradigm for self-improving agents. Current evaluations score the co-evolved policy on the final bank it trained with (the delivered bank). After deployment, however, skills may be rewritten, added or removed more frequently than the policy model is retrained, leaving the policy to operate on a drifted skill bank that neither the training objective nor existing evaluation protocols address. In this paper, we first establish, through theoretical and empirical analysis, that the fragility hidden by this blind spot is not incidental. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20867v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a general declarative framework for anticipatory reasoning about interactive motion in complex dynamic environments. Our focus is on (explainable) anticipatory space-time mental model formation at a semantic level to heuristically guide low-level motion computation. Our method is hybrid, modular and elaboration tolerant integrating: 1) An ASP model characterising the dynamics of interactive motion trajectories; 2) Semantically-guided prediction for deriving `branching trajectory futures'; and 3) An energy-based {optimisation} model to evaluate, rank and filter anticipations. We evaluate with the Argoverse 2 benchmark, where each anticipated trajectory carries an explicit, inspectable event-level hypothesis, unlike end-to-end stochastic prediction.

articles.title: A Multi-Tiered AI Accessibility Model (MAIAM): Proportionate Access and Capability Limits for Comprehensive Frontier AI Safety
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20921v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most debate about releasing capable AI systems treats the choice as binary: keep the model behind an API, or publish the weights. That framing runs together two separate decisions. One is how capable a system may become. The other is who may obtain a given capability, and on what terms. This paper is about the second decision. We propose a Multi-Tiered AI Accessibility Model (MAIAM) that sorts access by purpose, safety, and capability instead of by release artifact. Tier 1, AI for Learning, is broadly accessible and deliberately capability-bounded. Tier 2, AI for Exploration, serves research and development under registration, identity, and usage controls that tighten as capability rises. Tier 3, Full-Scale Frontier AI, is available only through structured, recorded, and accountable access. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20922v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Compositional structure is pervasive in nature and across scales: atoms combine into molecules, molecules into cells, and cells into organisms, while further compositional hierarchies appear within each level. More broadly, compositionality, the reuse and recombination of parts into novel structures, is a fundamental source of interesting complexity in both natural and artificial systems. Yet despite its importance, and despite our apparent ease in recognizing it, mathematical accounts capturing what we intuitively mean by compositional structure remain limited. Here, we fill this gap by formalizing a simple idea: compositional structure emerges when parts, considered together, reveal shared structure that is not captured when those parts are modeled separately. Abstract: Research on deceptive alignment is becoming increasingly urgent as frontier-model capabilities advance and their risk of causing catastrophic harm increases. Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is credited with gains beyond the domain its rewards check, such as higher MMLU accuracy after training on mathematics. Abstract: Global streamflow forecasting supports flood preparedness, yet data-driven models trained on reanalysis lose skill when driven by operational forecasts, increasingly so with lead time. AIFL addresses this shift with a two-stage transfer-learning recipe and a deterministic LSTM, but it feeds one forecast lead time into the whole input window and gives no uncertainty. Abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are typically trained on hundreds of millions to billions of activation tokens, yet little work has tested whether this scale is necessary. Abstract: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) compresses the content of a key-value cache into a shared latent per token, making low-bit storage attractive for long-context inference. Abstract: Residual context is key to unlocking the speed-quality Pareto frontier of diffusion language models (DLMs) by carrying forward predictive distributions across denoising steps. Yet turning this seemingly simple mechanism into an effective learning paradigm is far from simple: there is no clear recipe for how residual context should be learned. We introduce ORL, a framework for on-policy residual learning in DLMs. Algorithmically, we identify that residual learning is inherently on-policy. ORL learns from model-induced residual trajectories on the fly and introduces an entropy-contraction objective that sharpens predictions as the model revisits its own predictions. Abstract: Quantile forecasts summarize uncertainty at each future time step, while diffusion forecasters represent it through sampled future trajectories. We study how predicted quantiles can serve as distributional controls for diffusion forecasting. Specifically, we investigate how the mechanism of quantile integration affects its effectiveness in guiding a pretrained diffusion forecaster. We find that residual control throughout the denoising network yields the most consistent improvements. We instantiate this approach as Control-TS, which learns a quantile-control pathway while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen. Across eight benchmarks, Control-TS consistently improves the backbone's CRPS, achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art forecasting models, and retains its gains in capacity-matched comparisons. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) trained on vast amounts of data have demonstrated impressive performance over a range of tasks, but future performance gains will require increasing amounts of data and compute. Federated Learning (FL) facilitates training on decentralized private data, but client resource limitations can make training impractical, particularly as model sizes continue to expand. Abstract: Compact representations that support geometrically meaningful comparisons are valuable for learning from probability distributions. We study optimal, free-weight $M$-atom quantization of one-dimensional probability measures in quadratic Wasserstein distance and extend it to higher dimensions via slicing. articles.content:

Abstract: Understanding why listeners enjoy music is difficult because the experience is subjective and changes as a piece unfolds. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive way to study neural responses during listening, yet earlier work has mostly treated music emotion as a categorical label or relied on black-box models. We formulate enjoyment prediction as a regression problem on the public MUSIN-G dataset, which contains 128-channel EEG from 20 listeners together with song-level enjoyment ratings. Six deep learning models were compared under a participant-wise protocol, in which 15 listeners were used for training and validation and 5 were held out for testing. DeepConvNet, CNN-LSTM and GNN-CNN reached the lowest mean absolute error (0.97 to 0.99 on the 1 to 5 scale), while the temporal convolutional network (TCN) had the highest Pearson correlation with the ratings (r = 0.21). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20628v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) based on large language models (LLMs) have become a powerful way to address complex problems, and their effectiveness depends critically on the collaboration topology that decides which agents participate and how they communicate. Recent work learns to generate this topology from the task query, fitting the generator to corpora of execution-verified graphs. The post-training method for such generators remains a limitation: a corpus lists the graphs that solved a query but never ranks them, leaving continued supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with no per-query preference to exploit. Without such a preference, the generator drifts toward the topologies the corpus contains most often rather than those that suit each query, so a gain on one task can come at a cost on another. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long chain-of-thought decoding is memory-bound: the KV cache of the generated tokens grows linearly with the test-time compute being spent. Evicting cache entries does not fix this, because a model never trained on a cache with entries removed generates longer, often up to the length limit. We instead train the model to compress its own output. AbridgeKV compresses each completed block of generated text into the KV entries of a few learned pause tokens. These are extra input tokens with trained embeddings that produce no output. Once the pause tokens have encoded the block, AbridgeKV frees the block's original cache; subsequent tokens attend to the pause tokens' KV entries in its place. Abstract: Full-duplex spoken language models decide at every frame whether to take the floor, defining a conversational personality -- yet each set of weights encodes exactly one, which human speakers bracket rather than share. We identify it: a single late-layer residual-stream direction, the initiative vector, extracted from the model's own conversations without training or annotation. Abstract: Wolof is spoken by 23M people, mostly in Senegal, but remains weakly supported by open-weight language models, while API models raise cost, governance, and sovereignty constraints for local deployments. In this paper, we present 0.6B-14B open-weight models adapted to Wolof through instruction tuning, preference alignment, and model merging. Abstract: Reasoning distillation requires chain-of-thought (CoT) data with correct answers, but obtaining such data efficiently remains challenging. Forward CoT generation (FCG) followed by rejection sampling (RS) produces verified, question-only responses, yet may require many teacher calls for difficult problems. Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents rely on context compaction: when the interaction history outgrows the context window, a compressor replaces it with a natural-language summary. We show that these summaries contain more than a record of what happened. Compaction prompts ask for decisions and next steps, so each summary mixes facts established by the environment with reasoning written by the compressor, and the agent cannot tell the two apart afterwards. In an analysis of a widely used structured compressor, 83% of failed runs trace back to an action that carries out a specific summary entry, most of which no environment output supports. We propose Source-Judged Compaction (SJC), a training-free post-processing step that scores each summary entry for whether it has a source in the environment outputs or the previous summary, and removes the entries that do not. articles.title: BD-HazardVLM: Probing Vision-Language Models for Latent Defensive-Driving Hazards in Bangladesh Road Scenes
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20627v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly used for driving-scene understanding, yet their defensive reasoning under weakly structured Global South traffic remains unclear. We introduce BD-HazardVLM, a diagnostic benchmark of 500 Bangladesh road-scene images, comprising 375 from RSUD20K and 125 from TFP-BD, annotated for hazard presence, primary hazard category, risk timing, severity, defensive actions, visible evidence, and hallucination- and Western-road-bias traps. We evaluate Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B, and MiniCPM-V-4.6 using a shared zero-shot task definition and structured output schema. Binary hazard-presence accuracy ranges from 88.0 percent to 89.2 percent, essentially matching the 89.0 percent majority-class baseline. Fine-grained reasoning is substantially weaker: category accuracy remains below 40 percent, risk-timing accuracy ranges from 1.6 percent to 12.4 percent, and exact defensive-action matching remains below 2 percent.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20651v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Creating digital garments from existing two-dimensional patterns remains a time-consuming process. Although patterns are widely available in digital form, their assembly in garment CAD software involves manual definition of sewing operations and arrangement of the pattern panels for drape simulation. We present two learning-based approaches that automate both tasks using the 2D vector pattern as their sole input. Our automatic sewing model operates at the segment level, leveraging a Transformer encoder with multiple prediction heads. Our novel architecture supports many-to-many, ordered segment correspondences, as well as hems, overlapping seams needed for multilayer garments, and construction properties such as seam allowances and stitch types, required for the finished virtual garment but neglected by previous methods. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20693v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. Existing benchmarks assess selected geometric properties or use vision-language models to judge memory and consistency, leaving systematic 3D evaluation underexplored. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans interpret multimodal observations of the world and forecast how it will evolve. Recent multimodal generative systems have demonstrated similar capabilities: they can integrate multimodal context and synthesize visual outputs that depict changes in the world. To characterize this emerging trajectory, we organize model capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and discover that higher-level tasks remain relatively underexplored despite model progress. To bridge this gap, we explore model performance on multi-step world state prediction, a high-level task that requires models to forecast successive future world states from multimodal observations and diverse references. Such a task requires models to possess entangled understanding and generation capabilities, as well as extensive world knowledge to translate human action sequences, physical transformations, and abstract visual reasoning into coherent visual outputs. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20761v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Representation alignment improves and accelerates diffusion training by encouraging intermediate features to match a pretrained visual encoder. However, standard alignment matches pretrained representations without distinguishing what information may be more useful for generation. We introduce local appearance purification (LAP), which improves generation quality and makes encoders such as MAE more effective alignment targets by removing locally predictable content and aligning to the residual. LAP modifies only the alignment target, and requires no changes to diffusion training or inference. Through controlled interventions within a fixed encoder, we show that effective alignment depends on what information the target emphasizes, not simply how much image information it contains. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20781v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Image-to-text (I2T) understanding and text-to-image (T2I) generation are dual tasks in unified multimodal models (UMMs). Reconstructive post-training couples these tasks, but existing reconstruction-based methods remain perception-centric and provide limited supervision for reasoning about structure, intent, and transformation. We propose ReasonUni, a reasoning-augmented reconstructive post-training framework that extends this coupling beyond perception. Given an original image and an editing instruction, the UMM first reasons about what and how to edit and describes the target state, then generates the corresponding target image conditioned on this understanding output. To jointly optimize both modules, we introduce TreeGRPO, a tree-structured reinforcement learning method that samples multiple reasoning paths and candidate images per path, then aggregates visual rewards to update both modules under a unified objective. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20794v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent reinforcement learning approaches have improved visual text generation, yet generated images still suffer from incorrect wording and malformed glyphs. We identify two coupled limitations: recognition-based rewards often overlook visible glyph defects, while whole-image scalar feedback obscures the uneven quality of individual text regions. These limitations motivate our central principle: $\textit{Blame errant words, not the canvas}$, to effectively preserve local quality distinctions. First, we introduce $\mathbf{TextDART}$, a defect-aware region-targeted reward model that localizes individual text regions and independently evaluates their semantic correctness and glyph quality, providing fine-grained, region-precise feedback. Abstract: Generative gameplay requires more than immediate responses to player actions.Actions should have persistent consequences, while the generated world should act according to its own state and rules, shaping the player's situation and subsequent choices. Video generation captures local dynamics, but limited history, partially observed game state, and the need for contextual behavior decisions make such interactions difficult to sustain through audiovisual prediction alone. Abstract: Unified multimodal generation covers discrete, continuous, and hybrid paradigms. Discrete approaches with single-codebook visual tokenizers align naturally with text modeling but have limited representational capacity. Continuous and hybrid approaches retain richer visual representations, but they model text and images in heterogeneous spaces with different training objectives, potentially introducing optimization conflicts between modalities with misaligned representation spaces. These choices expose a central question: how to efficiently model high-capacity visual representations alongside textual content in a shared optimization space within a single backbone. Abstract: Map generation tasks feature extensive non-structural vectorized data (e.g., points, polylines, and polygons) and thus pose significant challenges to common pixel-wise generative models. Conventional approaches use multiple stages, first segmenting these features at the pixel level and then performing vectorized post-processing, with errors and complexity compounding at each stage. Motivated by the recent success of auto-regressive language modeling, we propose the first map foundation model, named Map Auto-Regressor (MARS), that is capable of generating both multi-polyline road networks and polygon buildings in a unified manner. For training MARS, we collected to our knowledge the largest multi-class map extraction dataset totaling 3.4M examples, which we call MAP-3M. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20852v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Negation is a fundamental aspect of language understanding and it is important vision-language models (VLMs) are able to process it effectively. We investigate how VLMs process negation by analysing attention patterns of different models. We draw comparisons between human gaze and attention in models when processing affirmative vs negated statements. We compare object level model attention to human eye-fixations in both binary and multary settings, evaluating with both synthetic and realistic datasets. We find models generally do not follow human-like attention patterns when resolving negation, suggesting they rely on mechanisms outside of attention. While layerwise analysis shows that PaliGemma2-3B shifts object attention to the alternative under negation, our headwise ablations suggest this is a byproduct rather than a negation processing mechanism. Abstract: Insect-induced defoliation threatens grapevine health and yield, yet severity assessment relies on subjective manual scouting. We developed DefoliationCAM (D-CAM), a solar-powered edge AI system that estimates canopy defoliation and transmits results via LoRa to a web dashboard. The pipeline uses YOLOX-Nano to localize grapevine cordons in 4K images and a MobileNet-based classifier with lightweight channel attention to classify 320 x 320 pixel patches. The 29,674 field-collected patches were labeled as background or one of four damage levels: no to negligible, mild, moderate, and severe. Merging moderate and severe classes reduced the class imbalance ratio from approximately 40:1 to 8.8:1. Synthetic augmentation increased macro-F1 from 0.768 to 0.838. Abstract: While foundation models and vision transformers (ViTs) have redefined visual representations, current active learning (AL) strategies for these backbones largely operate at the patch or region level, where annotation requirements remain high due to extensive pixel labeling. We introduce TEAL (Token-space Efficient Active Learning), the first pixel-level AL framework built around ViT representations. Abstract: Occupancy predictors rely on large persistent banks of Gaussians or learned queries whose size is fixed by hand. Abstract: Existing long-document QA benchmarks rarely combine large-scale human-authored questions with detailed visual evidence annotations, limiting diagnosis of evidence localization and interpretation failures. It contains 15,000 fully human-authored question-answer pairs across 5,859 real-world PDFs totaling 372,445 pages, balancing chart, table, and complex-layout tasks. Human annotations identify supporting pages and evidence elements and describe cited visual content, enabling separate retrieval and interpretation evaluation. Abstract: Geo-foundation models (GFMs) are typically evaluated by downstream task predictive performance, revealing little about which physical features they are sensitive to or use in prediction. Abstract: Spatial agents have access to reconstruction and segmentation tools, yet inconsistent predictions and fragmented object identities can prevent their outputs from becoming reliable 3D scene information. Abstract: Diffusion models are notoriously expensive to train, requiring large-scale datasets to learn how to gradually reverse the noise from images over multiple small denoising steps. Abstract: Damage-recovery algorithms often rank gaits from short trials, yet a gait that performs well briefly may not remain effective during continued execution. In particular, the methodology introduced in this work addresses the use of sustainably powered autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) to perform scientific missions that prioritize locations of maximum interest. Because these locations of maximum interest are not known a priori but are rather identified based on in-situ measurements, online adaptation is essential for mission planning. articles.content:

Abstract: Vehicles that lose control at the handling limit through icing, hydroplaning, or an abrupt evasive maneuver fall outside the operating envelope of production safety systems such as electronic stability control, which focus on preventing instability rather than recovering from it. Expert drivers regain authority in these conditions by drifting. Existing autonomous recovery approaches are validated on idealized scenarios, define "recovered" states empirically and inconsistently, or rely on offline-planned trajectories rather than acting online. We address these gaps by first training a racing policy with reinforcement learning that learns drifting as a time-optimal maneuver, then adapting it to recovery through continued training with a minimum-time reward. Abstract: Sustainably powered mobile robots enable long-duration observational missions by harvesting energy from the environment. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20895v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Satisfying safety constraints for systems with second-order dynamics is challenging because a position constraint may require infeasible deceleration. Higher-order control barrier functions (CBFs) provide an approach for expressing safety conditions for such systems but feasibility depends on the system dynamics and available control authority. We develop a constructive approach for designing feasible safety constraints for second-order control-affine systems. Starting from a signed distance function (SDF), we construct collision-free spheres, i.e., bubbles, in position space, and use their quadratic geometry and overlap to construct a velocity-dependent safety constraint. The associated safe set is represented as a union of intersections and enforced through a quadratic-program safety filter. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20901v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Task-Oriented Grasping (TOG) has emerged as an important skill for purposeful robotic manipulation. Given the task of using a knife to "slice bread," a robot must choose to grasp from the handle, whereas for "hand[ing] the knife over," it is preferable for the handle to remain unobstructed for safe handoff. Current approaches for TOG either focus on 2D planar grasping, remain limited by their reliance on task-agnostic grasp generators, or are constrained by reliance on finite, manually-annotated, task-specific grasp datasets that cannot cover all possible grasp-task pairs. To that end, we present TGrasp6D, a vision-language based approach for generating task-oriented 6DoF grasps in a zero-shot manner. Abstract: Egocentric human videos offer a scalable alternative to costly robot demonstra- tions, yet transferring their manipulation priors to robot control remains chal- lenging. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robust adaptive control is vital for keeping robots safe while actively reducing uncertainty in unfamiliar settings. However, traditional methods are often conservative since they fail to account for guaranteed future parameter learning during planning and struggle to scale to high-dimensional systems. In this work, we present A-SLS, a learning-aware robust adaptive model predictive control (RAMPC) framework based on system-level synthesis. A-SLS forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between process disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to construct tight, guaranteed reachable sets that account for future information gain. We also develop a GPU-accelerated A-SLS solver to enable real-time performance. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20936v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generating dynamically feasible motions for legged and manipulating robots requires solving a large, nonlinear, non-convex optimal control problem (OCP) in which contact wrenches must satisfy friction-cone constraints throughout the motion, not only at isolated instants. Existing solvers are sensitive to the initial guess and scale poorly with the number of joints. This paper introduces LEAP, which transcribes the OCP with pseudospectral collocation and, instead of a Newton or SQP solve, integrates a primal--dual gradient flow of a Powell--Hestenes--Rockafellar augmented Lagrangian to compute a solution. Because the flow is stiff, this paper designs a linearly implicit integrator with a Gauss--Newton metric, momentum, and a merit-based step controller that keeps the augmented Lagrangian monotone. Abstract: Accurate trajectory tracking is essential for autonomous underwater vehicles operating with uncertain hydrodynamics and limited thruster authority. articles.title: When a robot can trust reversing wind to find an odour source
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A wind-derived heading can guide a robot towards an odour source even after the wind reverses, but its reliability depends on the plume's transport history. On a quadruped initially facing the source, holding the initial heading reached it in every reversing-wind trial, whereas comparison controllers never settled there. An exact geometric condition links heading correctness to net odour transport, and simulations separate sensing error from departures from nominal flow. Where the alternating wind directions are too close for reversal alone to produce wrong-side headings, the wrong-side rate rises from 1.0% under uniform transport to 4.7% in a stochastic flow. Re-acquiring headings from new odour contact improves simulated search when contact is intermittent. These results identify distinct requirements for wind-guided search: a heading supported by the transport geometry and sufficient intermittent contact to replace it.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Passive human videos of everyday activity offer robots access to a massive amount of human experience without requiring a demonstration for each task. However, using this experience requires recovering knowledge from unstructured video recordings and adapting it to a different body (i.e., the robot). To overcome these challenges, we present mobile code-as-policy (MoCaP), an agentic framework that turns passive human video recordings into guidance for an end-to-end mobile manipulation policy. MoCaP extracts spatial memory and cues of how people prepare to interact with objects, which inform navigation and the search for a manipulation-ready configuration. Guided by passive human experience and current observations, MoCaP uses a closed-loop code-as-policy to coordinate planning and tool use primitives to solve motions under the robot's geometry and kinematic constraints. articles.title: Slip-Induced Fall Suppression During Cornering for a Remotely Operated Motorcycle with a Rear-Wheel-Swing Mechanism
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.21089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Slip-induced falls when riding motorcycles are difficult to avoid even for expert riders and represent a major cause of single-vehicle accidents. Despite their prevalence, no practical solution has yet been proposed to suppress this phenomenon. We previously introduced a motorcycle model applicable to systems with both front- and rear- wheel steering. In this paper, we extend that model and formulate the suppression of slip-induced falls as an optimization problem that distributes assistive control inputs according to vehicle speed and road surface conditions. To evaluate the proposed method, we developed a remotely operated motorcycle and conducted experiments under two scenarios: slalom driving on a low-friction surface at 5.5 m/s, and turning maneuvers on synthetic ice to simulate driving over manholes on rainy days. The results demonstrate that our approach successfully suppresses falls under these challenging conditions.

articles.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
articles.content: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.

articles.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
articles.content: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of video generative pretraining for unified 4D perception. See https://gen4p.github.io for more visual results.

articles.title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
articles.content: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. Existing method addresses this by preserving prompt-aligned foreground regions, thereby protecting semantically relevant structures. However, this text-relevance criterion overlooks background objects, local details that are not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, leading to degraded structural coherence. In this work, we propose Dynamics-aware Token Merging (DaTMe), a training-free framework that grounds token merging in the underlying diffusion dynamics. Our key insight is that token importance should reflect whether a token remains unresolved during denoising and whether it carries structural information. To this end, DaTMe constructs a dynamics- aware importance map from the Tweedie denoised estimate. The map combines a temporal signal, measuring inter-step changes in the predicted clean image, with a structural signal, capturing local high-frequency content such as boundaries and fine details. Using this map, DaTMe adaptively assigns tokens into merging roles under a given compression ratio: important tokens are preserved as anchors, while tokens that are both temporally stabilized and structurally homogeneous are selected as safe merge candidates. Experiments on PixArt-a and FLUX demonstrate that DaTMe maintains visual fidelity across the entire image, highlighting diffusion dynamics as an effective token-level merging decision in efficient generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/SeungJuCha/DaTMe.

articles.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
articles.content: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. Dynamic caching methods decide when to refresh by accumulating a cheap probe of the network input into a staleness signal and spending a fresh evaluation once it crosses a threshold. They perform hard caching: the signal is a binary switch between refresh and reuse, and every step, fresh or cached, advances by the prescribed step size. We observe that the signal carries much more than this switch. How far it sits below the threshold, its headroom, predicts the error induced by reuse. We propose SoftCache, which performs soft caching: instead of a binary switch, the headroom sets how far each cached step goes. Where the headroom is large, the sampler jumps past several scheduled nodes, and as a refresh nears, its steps shrink back toward the original step. These adaptive jumps may land between the scheduled nodes, taking the sampler off its fixed grid. SoftCache requires no training and adds no per-backbone settings: on FLUX for images and on HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 for video, at speedups from $3.5\times$ to $6.9\times$, it is ahead of every baseline on all four fidelity metrics.

articles.title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies
articles.content: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. We present Value as Memory (VaM), a framework that addresses these challenges through value caching and online real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. Across long-horizon tasks involving deformable objects and contact-rich manipulation, VaM yields a mean absolute success-rate gain of $29.4\%$ with value caching, while achieving a $32.8\%$ gain with online autonomous learning over matched offline training. The evaluated online schedule performs $8\times$ as many policy iterations under the same gradient-step budget, with more than $2\times$ lower recorded time per gradient step with concurrent data collection and training.

articles.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
articles.content: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.

articles.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
articles.content: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

articles.title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets, while producing goal-directed manipulation videos with stronger instruction adherence and action progression than video-generation baselines. Project Page: https://p3-wam.pages.dev/

articles.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
articles.content: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.

articles.title: Grounding Generative Verification in 3D Content
articles.content: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and 3D generation have expanded 3D understanding and synthesis. However, beyond visual fidelity, task-specific correctness grounded in 3D evidence remains a major challenge. We argue that building reliable 3D systems requires not only stronger generation and reasoning, but also verification feedback that identifies unmet requirements and explains their violations, allowing systems to reflect on and refine their outputs. Such feedback must integrate multi-view observations and distinguish genuine inconsistencies from projection-dependent appearances. We make three contributions. First, we introduce 3DVerifierBench, a benchmark spanning 10 tasks that evaluates decisions, rejection explanations, and responses to controlled changes in specifications and candidates. A human study reveals a 21.6 percentage-point gap between humans and the strongest tested model, GPT-6 Astra, while explanation-aware analysis exposes weaknesses in rejection reliability. Second, we analyze verification across fine-grained factual categories, exposing errors in values and target binding. We develop a scalable pipeline combining multi-view fact extraction, controlled 3D editing, and native annotations to produce 14,126 training examples with contradiction explanations and linked counterfactuals. Third, we examine how verification could support 3D generation through candidate selection and recursive refinement. In human-labeled sixteen-candidate pools, oracle selection improves complete factual success from 26.7% to 90.0%. In a separate eight-input study, human-guided recursive refinement satisfies all seven requirements for every input, compared with three under parallel Oracle@8. Together, our benchmark, analysis, and data pipeline establish a foundation for models to reflect on 3D content through reliable verification feedback.

articles.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
articles.content: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws. Together, these enable PathFM to generate multiple paths for a single series in roughly the time needed for one query to a quantile model. The distilled sampler also makes it practical to optimize a calibration loss directly. PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on the established forecasting benchmarks fev-bench and TIME. To complement these evaluations, we introduce Forecast Path Score Bench (fps-bench), which augments fev-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics. PathFM achieves a higher aggregate path score on fps-bench than all evaluated external baselines. Experiments on chaotic systems further show that our flow model sustains long-run variability, while strong baselines rapidly collapse. PathFM makes generative time series forecasting both competitive and practical, enabling diverse downstream applications.

articles.title: DK-VLM: Geometry as Position for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
articles.content: Vision-language models still struggle to understand 3D spatial relations across views and update spatial judgments as the observer moves. A common approach fuses 3D reconstruction features into visual tokens, but aligning these features with pretrained semantic representations remains challenging under limited spatial supervision. We propose DK-VLM with Dual-Kernel Attention, which computes attention from both a visual token's input position and its geometric position in the scene. A semantic kernel retains the pretrained model's native attention and positional encoding, while a separate geometric kernel uses estimated 3D points and camera poses to directly modulate attention through point displacements and relative view transformations. Then, a learned gate fuses their outputs. Geometry thus enters attention as position rather than as fused reconstruction features. We further introduce Reference-Frame Composition (RC) supervision to train the model to update its reference frame across successive judgments. It provides stepwise turn and heading targets derived from verified single-step annotations. Among the compared methods, DK-VLM-8B achieves the highest average score across six spatial benchmarks and the highest overall scores on VSI-Bench (74.33) and ReVSI-32 (58.28). RC supervision further improves multi-step spatial reasoning, while the full model preserves general video understanding. Project page: https://sumuru789.github.io/DK-VLM-website/.

articles.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
articles.content: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique signal. Our experiments further demonstrate that these structured and interpretable outputs improve the verifier's generalization to out-of-domain multimodal critic tasks. To train this verifier, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise local feedback to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable continuous scoring at the global level. Under a general reinforcement learning framework, we first empirically demonstrate that the proposed pointwise graded verifier significantly outperforms binary verifiers in traditional text-to-image scenarios. We then extend our investigation to rule-governed generative world modeling where generative models are leveraged for world simulation and world reasoning under explicit rules. From a theoretical standpoint, we further show that a pairwise verification paradigm yields more accurate critiques than the pointwise formulation when ground-truth images are available, with empirical results on diverse structured world-modeling tasks such as Maze and Sudoku further validating the effectiveness of our approach. Overall, our findings suggest a key insight: the transition from generative models to structured world-modeling agents critically hinges on the availability of accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers.

articles.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
articles.content: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models have become an important approach for scaling model parameters. Modern MoE architectures increasingly combine two design choices: fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts. The former increases expressiveness by enabling more expert combinations at a fixed activation ratio, and the latter introduces experts that are active for every token. We identify an exploration dilemma between these designs: shared experts can make routing less exploratory by reducing the variability of token representations. This conflicts with the greater need for exploration induced by fine-grained expert segmentation due to the combinatorially enlarged routing space. Consequently, the additional expressiveness offered by fine-grained segmentation may not be fully realized in practice. MirrorMoE is proposed to reconcile this exploration dilemma by shrinking the exploration space through token-adaptive suppression of unnecessary experts. MirrorMoE consistently improves performance across model scales.

articles.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
articles.content: Single image 3D generation aims to dress a given 3D mesh with relightable materials while faithfully preserving the visual details of a reference image. Existing methods either introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or struggle to preserve fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning. To resolve these challenges, we introduce SUPRA-Tex, built on the principle of decoupling visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion. This division of labor allows the 3D generator, trained on limited 3D data, to focus its capacity on preserving visible evidence and completing unobserved surfaces. Specifically, we first train an MLLM-based image editing model to predict lighting-separated PBR maps in the reference view. We then project these maps onto the visible surface and encode them with the pretrained material VAE encoder into native observation latents that share the generation target's latent space. An interleaved flow transformer holds these latents as fixed, read-only anchors while alternating unobserved-region and full-surface updates to generate complete material latents. This design achieves super-alignment with the reference, delivering What You See Is What You Get fidelity on visible regions and coherent completion on unobserved surfaces. Trained solely on public datasets, SUPRA-Tex achieves SOTA performance in both geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end asset generation, matching or even exceeding leading commercial systems on in-the-wild images. Project page: https://supra-3d.github.io/supratex/

articles.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
articles.content: Existing agent benchmarks typically evaluate agents on well-specified tasks defined by issue reports, specifications, or task tickets. Real-world customer delivery is different: forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must clarify ambiguous requirements, work in live systems, and uncover unstated constraints. We introduce FDE-Gym, a benchmark of 95 end-to-end delivery tasks from 20 customer scenarios across 18 sectors, each adapted by industry experts from real-world delivery projects. In simulated customer environments with scripted stakeholders and modifiable customer systems, agents interact with stakeholders and operate on production-like systems to deliver working solutions. FDE-Gym scores a delivery by how much it improves the customer's own success metric, normalized between 0 (unchanged system) and 1 (reference solution), with penalties for stakeholder interactions (messages, trial runs, and waiting time). An online platform lets humans practice FDE skills under the same grading criteria. We evaluate 13 model configurations from seven providers. In the realistic setting, where unstated constraints must be discovered, the best configuration achieves a mean FDE-Gym score of 0.56 and resolves only 14 of the 95 tasks (a score of at least 0.8 with no incident). Discovering unstated constraints is the primary bottleneck: performance drops sharply when models must uncover them without explicit guidance. Yet information discovery alone does not account for the gap: even on the 23 tasks where the best configuration obtains every key fact from stakeholders, it reaches a normalized business uplift of 0.8 or above on only 10. These results reveal a substantial gap between solving well-specified tasks and delivering effective AI systems for real customers.
